*Generated by `tools/benchmark_alignment.py`, total runtime 173.2s. Grounded in `docs/research/alignment-algorithm-survey.md` sections 5-6.*

> **Run provenance (2026-07-18):** this run was executed on the CORRECTED library templates —
> after the template axis-canonicalization fix (loader now trusts the verified saved axis) and
> the winner-only re-centering. It **supersedes the pre-fix run of 2026-07-14**, whose S0
> baseline measured templates tilted 4–88° off their true axis; numbers from that run are
> indicative only and must not be quoted. Headline shifts on the corrected templates: seat
> failures collapsed from 31/170 to 2/153 gesture rows (S0/S2/S3), the physical rim-band bound
> rose from 86.3% to 95.4% (S0) and 89.2% to 99.3% (S3), and curated-click fidelity tightened

> rejecting derived gestures, not a template defect.

## Data caveat (read first)

Every real site under `data/real/scans/*/sites.json` carries a `(center_mark, rim_mark)` PAIR (a single radius measurement), never a `rim_points` array of 3+ discrete clicks. **Protocol B's literal selection rule ("every site with >=4 rim_points") matches 0 real sites** (of 10 total). To still exercise Protocol B, an 8-point "curated click" gesture was DERIVED per site from the doctor's measured radius plus the scan's own rim band (the same band construction `auto_flow._rim_seat` fits a plane through) — grounded in real surface geometry, not fabricated on a perfect circle. **10 sites got a derived gesture** and are reported with `gesture_source="derived"` throughout the JSON; every row is labeled so native vs. derived gestures are never conflated. Treat Protocol B's results as measuring robustness of the SEATING algorithms under a realistic-but-synthetic multi-click gesture, not as a native reproduction of a doctor's actual border clicks (which this dataset does not contain).

## Which is the better fit — vs. the S0 baseline

S1 (GNC-robust circle) is a narrowly-scoped, cheap upgrade: it only touches the circle fit that feeds the SAME `_pinned_rim_seat` production function, so any stability gain over S0 under single-outlier-click gestures is attributable directly to the annealed weighting rather than a different seating objective. S2 (joint click+surface, bounded trust region) and S3 (dense constrained grid) both re-seat from scratch inside an explicit +-12deg/+-1.5mm (S2) or +-9deg/+-1.5mm (S3) trust region around the S0 seed — per the survey's mode-(c) warning, neither is a free-roaming optimizer, so a stability win (or loss) here reflects the shape of THAT bounded objective, not an unconstrained ICP wandering into a different basin.

On this dataset, S1's median 1.2mm-outlier axis tilt (3.09 deg) is **more stable than** S0's own (6.41 deg) under the SAME derived-gesture protocol.

Protocol C variant identification: S0-production-pinned achieved 0% top-1 exact accuracy on 4 labeled sites. IMPORTANT NUANCE: this benchmark's S0 mirrors only production's PINNED-seat path (`_fit_circle_3d` + `_pinned_rim_seat`, a rigid 1.2mm-residual contract) — production's actual `run_auto_case`, on these SAME 2-point-mark sites, instead uses the FREE `_rim_seat` path (no rigid pin, a 1-D depth search). Production's own no-declaration (AUTO) accuracy on the labeled arches is a MOVING number that must be re-measured per code state — do not cite a figure from this generated doc; the current verified measurement lives in docs/research/alignment-confidence-roadmap.md (and note the product now REQUIRES the doctor's declaration at intake, which drives 4/4-correct alignment, so AUTO accuracy is a cross-check property, not the shipping path). The height-twin observability limit the survey documents as mode (d) applies regardless. `_pinned_rim_seat` additionally refuses to seat the true 7030 template at all against this benchmark's DERIVED 8-click gesture (see the data caveat above), which is why S0-production-pinned's Protocol C table above cannot even RANK 7030 for that site — a property of feeding the pinned path a derived gesture it was not calibrated for, layered on top of the pre-existing height-twin limit. The alternative strategies (S1-S3) rank variants by their OWN seat residual (never the calibrated symmetric score S0 was tuned against, per the task's explicit instruction not to touch that contract), so a lower Protocol C accuracy for S1/S2/S3 here reflects an un-calibrated ranking objective, not necessarily worse geometry — this is exactly the survey's rule-1 warning ("never score with the objective being optimized") applied to a THIRD-PARTY ranking rule the alternatives were never tuned against.

## Caveats

- **No absolute pose ground truth on real arches.** Per the survey's metrology section (6), stability under click perturbation, the physical rim-band bound, and the 4 labeled variant codes are PROXIES, not independent 6-DoF pose truth. A pose that scores well on all three can still be wrong in a dimension none of them probe (e.g. clocking, which distance metrics on these revolute-ish parts are blind to by design).
- **Protocol B's gestures are DERIVED, not native**, for every site except the 0 with a native >=4-point `rim_points` array (see the data caveat above) — treat the numbers as a controlled-perturbation robustness study on realistic synthetic gestures, not a replay of real doctor clicks.
- **Never compare `seat_residual` values ACROSS strategies** — S0/S1's pinned-seat residual, S2's Huber-loss objective and S3's trimmed-mean score are different objectives on different scales; only same-strategy, same-site comparisons (e.g. curated vs. perturbed) are meaningful, exactly per the survey's rule 1.
- **S3's grid is coarse by construction** (3deg tilt steps, 0.25mm height steps, refined +-1 step at half resolution) to keep total runtime bounded; a finer grid would likely narrow S3's residual further at proportionally higher cost.
- **S2/S3 are subsampled at the CLI level to fit the runtime budget** — S2 scores <= 700 patch points with max_nfev=60 (module defaults are 1500/200); S3 scores against a 900-point template sample with <= 700 patch points (module default is 1500/1500). Measured on a real site: this moves the seat residual by ~0.02mm and the pose by a fraction of a degree — noted here rather than applied silently. `src/case_prep/research/benchmark_strategies.py`'s own unit tests exercise the accuracy-tier (module-default) parameters; only this CLI's protocol runs use the faster settings.
- **S2/S3 seed from S0's pose** when no explicit seed is supplied (Protocol C runs each variant's own S0 seat first) — both are refinement strategies around a trusted seed, not independent global solvers (per the survey's explicit rejection of free 6-DoF/global registration as primary solver, section 3(c)).
- **Height-twin variants are an observability limit, not an optimizer failure** (survey mode d) — a strategy that ties two variants' seat residuals is behaving correctly; Protocol C's top-1 metric cannot express a tie and will penalize this correct behaviour identically to a genuine misidentification.
